productionFreezeProof.result: EMPTY - confirmed zero production-file change across all 8 Part B auditor commits (6ff1308, 0a8e8a4, c64f893, 0883407, bd8af72, 288fe07, 9e6a083, 70f8eff).

isolationDisciplineHeldForPartB: Every auditor was instructed to never run `prisma migrate dev`/`reset`/`db push`, to scope any test company/row to an exact fixed id, and to run scripts/check-destructive-db-patterns.ts before finishing. No auditor reported the guard finding anything new. Two benign git-index races occurred from 7 concurrent sessions sharing one worktree (a classic recurrence of this project's own documented hazard) - both were caught and cleanly resolved by the affected auditors themselves (bd8af72) or by the orchestrating session (9e6a083) without any data loss, and without ever touching the shared Postgres database destructively. This is qualitatively different from the incident this phase itself had to recover from: a git-index race over which agent's commit lands first is cheap to detect and resolve (nothing is lost, just reordered); a concurrent unguarded database reset is not.
conclusion: Part B's own required production-freeze-proof and crosscutting safety discipline both hold. Proceeding to final per-finding disposition and terminal verdict.
